[vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1453143684214{margin-top: 50px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="Webinars" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554307804024{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

BoardEffect is committed to providing quality resources to keep you up-to-date on the latest issues, trends and best practices in board management and governance. Below are our webinar event offerings! Sign up for free or watch old events on-demand.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vcex_divider][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1603289837560{margin-top: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="On-Demand:" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:left|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1603289872491{padding-top: 20px !important;padding-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Beyond the Boardroom: How Healthcare Systems are leveraging BoardEffect across their organizations" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:30|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1605105807384{padding-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]Join us as we (virtually) sit down with Brian Uy, Solution Architect at MemorialCare Health System, to discuss how his organization has been getting the most out of BoardEffect throughout the pandemic and their plans looking forward.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="https://go.boardeffect.com/WebinarBeyondtheBoardroom.html" title="Beyond the Boardroom Webinar" margin="top:20|right:20|bottom:20|left:20" css_wrap=".vc_custom_1604598748932{margin-top: 5px !important;}"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Cyber-Security in the Boardroom" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:30|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599056631850{padding-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]With cyber-security as daily headline news, we all know this is not just an issue for IT staff. Board members play a crucial role in setting policy, following good cyber practices, and ensuring that resources are sufficient to support cybersecurity operations. Get the information you need to be a cyber-savvy director.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="https://go.boardeffect.com/WebinarCybersecurityInTheBoardroom.html" title="Cyber-Security in the Boardroom Webinar" margin="top:20|right:20|bottom:20|left:20"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Bank on Security: How Credit Unions are Leveraging BoardEffect Tools" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:30|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599056978635{padding-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]Twin Star Credit Union and Conexus Credit Union join us to discuss the the benefits and pitfalls of technology, especially when it comes to highly secure industries such as financial services.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="https://learn.diligent.com/WebinarBankOnSecurity.html" title="Building a Diverse Board Webinar" margin="top:20|right:20|bottom:20|left:20" css_wrap=".vc_custom_1599057137907{margin-top: 5px !important;}"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1608050961202{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Tips & Tools for Building a Diverse Board Virtually" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:30|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599057087377{padding-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]Your non-profit board has committed to becoming more diverse, and is working hard to recruit and onboard new candidates. Stacey Woodland, CEO of YWCA Tri-County Area, joins us to discuss ways to harness digital tools to help you do this critical work.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="https://learn.diligent.com/WebinarBuildingDiverseBoardVirtually.html" title="Building a Diverse Board Webinar" margin="top:20|right:20|bottom:20|left:20" css_wrap=".vc_custom_1599057173478{margin-top: 10px !important;}"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Best Practices for Virtual Board Meetings During COVID-19" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:30|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599057539465{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]Human Rights Campaign's Mitch Johnson joins us as we discuss how to successfully conduct online meetings for your organization’s board – while maintaining good governance. In the webinar, we will discuss best practices for online meetings.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="https://learn.diligent.com/VirtualBoardMeetingsDuringCOVID19.html" title="Virtual Board Meetings Webinar" margin="top:20|right:20|bottom:20|left:20"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Five Ways to Streamline Healthcare Governance" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:30|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599057548218{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]Join BoardEffect and former American Hospital Association Vice President of Trustee Services, for a discussion about useful strategies, tips and tools to streamline your governance processes and foster greater board engagement.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="https://learn.diligent.com/WebinarFiveWaystoStreamlineHealthcareGovernanceNov.html" title="Five Ways to Streamline Healthcare Governance" margin="top:20|right:20|bottom:20|left:20"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1608050969749{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 10px !important;background-color: #ffffff !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Top 5 Governance Issues Facing Nonprofits for 2019" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599060025347{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]
A commitment to using the best practices around good governance can improve board leadership, benefiting the organization’s stakeholders. In this session we will dive into the top 5 governance challenges for 2019 and how to solve for them along with the Gulf Coast Community Foundation.
[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="https://www.boardeffect.com/governance-issues-facing-nonprofits/" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="The Pivotal Role of the Nonprofit Board Chair" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599060044447{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]
In this webinar, Anne Wallestad, CEO of BoardSource, and Vernetta Walker, BoardSource’s Chief Governance Officer and Vice President of Programs will delve into the findings from Boardsource's Leading with Intent study and share tips for creating a partnership with the executive and helping develop a strong board culture.
[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-pivotal-role-nonprofits-board-chair" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="How To Address Your Nonprofit’s Board Diversity" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599060052081{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]
Earlier in this webinar series, we looked into the findings from BoardSource’s 2017 report Leading with Intent, which highlighted that not only has board diversity declined, but that this is unlikely to change given that boards aren’t prioritizing demographics when recruiting even after nonprofits express dissatisfaction with their boards’ diversity.  In Part 2, we will dive into questions raised from that earlier session.
[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-address-your-nonprofits-board-diversity/" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1608050977415{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Stop the Revolving Door: CEO Succession Planning" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599060602484{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

Dottie Schindlinger moderates this 30-minute webinar interview with Dr. Kenneth Cohen and Mr. Ken Hanover of The Synergy Organization on evidenced-based models for CEO succession planning in hospitals and healthcare institutions.

[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-stop-revolving-door-ceo-succession-planning/" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Best Practices for Board Evaluations" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599060610241{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

Annual board self-evaluations have long been considered a best practice, with the idea that measuring board performance leads to continuous improvement in governance. In this webinar we discuss issues such as common flaws in board evaluation requirements issued by regulators and how most board evaluation processes impede change.

[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-best-practices-for-board-evaluations/" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Understanding Programs: A Great Unrecognized Correlate to Board Excellence" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599060059850{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]
In this webinar, we’ll delve into the findings from Leading with Intent to illustrate what you lose when your board fundamentally doesn’t understand the organization’s programs. We’ll share practical advice and guidance for how to provide members with ongoing opportunities to understand the organization’s mission and work. 
[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-understanding-programs-great-unrecognized-correlate-board-excellence" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1608050985133{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 10px !important;background-color: #ffffff !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Not Your Father’s Board Meeting- Tips for Structuring Must Attend Meetings" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599065048453{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]Are you frustrated by your directors’ lack of preparation for the meeting? Join BoardEffect and Terrie Temkin, Ph.D., Principal of CoreStrategies for Nonprofits to explore tools, tips, and technology designed to help your board work more efficiently and effectively.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-not-fathers-board-meeting-tips-structuring-must-attend-meetings/" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Top Pitfalls of Open Meeting Law: What your Charter School Board Needs to Know!" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599065855921{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

Join us for this introductory webinar featuring John Cairns Law and Beth Finch, founder of CharterSource, to explore common misconceptions of Open Meeting Law and how to help your board work more efficiently.

[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-top-pitfalls-open-meeting-law-2017-what-charter-school-board-needs-know" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Is Your Board Structured for Impact?" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599064959174{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]
Join Anne Wallestad, BoardSource’s CEO, Vernetta Walker, BoardSource’s Chief Governance Officer and VP of Programs, and Dr. David Renz, Director of the Midwest Center for Nonprofit Leadership at the University of Missouri-Kansas City to learn about the factors you should consider to determine the ideal size and structure for your board to advance your organization’s mission. 
[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-board-management-workshop-board-structured-impact/" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1608050992391{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="How to Get Your Board ``Onboard`` and Aligned" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599065466141{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]Your board members are an extension of your organization, and just like you and your team, they are best equipped to support and propel your mission forward when they are strategically aligned. However, this can often be easier said than done, which is why Plenty and BoardEffect have joined forces to guide you through this critical, and sometimes complex process. Join our teams for an exclusive webinar on how to create alignment with and within your board.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/webinar-how-to-get-board-aligned/" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="The Completely Revised Guide to Great Board Recruitment" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599065472924{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]Recruiting board members for many nonprofits is an exercise lacking not only in vision but in common sense. Nonprofits have been sold something of a bill of goods when it comes to board recruitment and this results in some all too familiar problems that repeat not only in the sector overall but in the same organizations over and over again. Join Vernetta Walker, VP of programs and Chief Governance Officer for BoardSource and Anasuya Sengupta, NPQ Board Member.[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="https://www.boardeffect.com/webinar-completely-revised-guide-to-great-board-recruitment/" size="medium" margin="20px" classes="green"]WATCH NOW![/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vc_custom_heading text="Generating Better Board Decisions" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1599065065070{margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

Join us for this brief webinar designed to help your board think differently. This session provides you with an overview of ways to re-frame problems and consider issues from multiple perspectives simultaneously as well as opportunities for robust discussion in board meetings – allowing space for board members to be curious, intrigued, and highly engaged.

item.content:encoded:
[vc_row column_spacing="60" equal_height="yes" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1555000211189{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 25px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_video link="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xZcpP6LW5dg" css=".vc_custom_1457101878730{margin-top: 50px !important;}"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1457102275466{margin-bottom: 100px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="The Completely Revised Guide to Great Board Recruitment" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:left|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes"][vc_column_text]

Recruiting board members for many nonprofits is an exercise lacking not only in vision but in common sense.

The truth is nonprofits have been sold something of a bill of goods when it comes to board recruitment and this results in some all too familiar problems that repeat not only in the sector overall but in the same organizations over and over again. About speakers: Vernetta Walker is vice president of programs and chief governance officer for BoardSource. She has worked with many national and international nonprofit organizations addressing a wide range of governance issues—from how to start a nonprofit organization to improving board engagement and performance to restructuring complex entities. Anasuya Sengupta has been on the Board of the Nonprofit Quarterly from August 2015. Her work so far has included supporting and strengthening free knowledge, human rights and social justice movements and communities of practice. Most recently, she created and headed the Grantmaking department (now Community Engagement) at the Wikimedia Foundation, supporting Wikimedia communities worldwide in their efforts to create and enable free and open knowledge. Before that, Anasuya was the Regional Program Director for Asia and the Pacific Islands, at the Global Fund for Women, one of the world's largest grant-making organisations exclusively for women's human rights. Lingering economic uncertainty, the need to accommodate millenials, and the ever-present challenge of recruiting and inspiring a diverse cast of new board members - those issues are making 2016 as challenging as ever for nonprofit boards.

BoardEffect's new report breaks down the 4 trends that experts see for this year and beyond along with suggestions for addressing them. The trends being:

item.title: How to Run a Board Meeting
item.dc:creator: Jbarlow
item.content:encoded:
[vc_row][vc_column][rev_slider_vc alias="082021-how-to-run-a-board-meeting"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1455895835887{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="New Guide: How to Run a Board Meeting" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%23194f7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1555961371616{margin-top: 75px !important;margin-bottom: 30px !important;}"][vc_custom_heading text="All the resources you need to run effective board meetings" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:25px|text_align:center" use_theme_fonts="yes"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1461760580929{margin-top: 30px !important;margin-bottom: 25px !important;}"]

Running a board meeting can be a complicated affair. Whether you are the board chair worrying about maintaining focus and facilitating engagement or the board liaison preoccupied with the difficulties of planning the meeting and creating board books, board meetings involve many carefully arranged parts and details.  This guide demystifies the challenges of running a board meeting by breaking it down into 3 helpful sections: Roles & Responsibilities, Running an Effective Meeting, and Board Meeting Procedures. Throughout we cover the basics and best practices in how to run a board of directors meeting.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="0px"][vc_column width="1/3"][vcex_button url="/how-to-run-a-board-meeting/#responsibilities" target="local" layout="expanded" title="Roles & Responsibilities" style="flat" align="center" font_family="Open Sans" text_transform="capitalize" custom_background="#194f7d" custom_hover_background="#00162d" custom_color="#ffffff" custom_hover_color="#ffffff" border_radius="0px" font_size="14px" letter_spacing="1px"]Roles & Responsibilities[/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vcex_button url="/how-to-run-a-board-meeting/#effective" target="local" layout="expanded" title="Running an Effective Board Meeting" style="flat" align="center" font_family="Open Sans" text_transform="capitalize" custom_background="aec03d" custom_hover_background="#667431" custom_color="#ffffff" custom_hover_color="#ffffff" border_radius="0px" font_size="14px" letter_spacing="1px"]Running an Effective Board Meeting[/vcex_button][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vcex_button url="/how-to-run-a-board-meeting/#procedures" target="local" layout="expanded" title="Board Meeting Procedures" style="flat" align="center" font_family="Open Sans" text_transform="capitalize" custom_background="#2d2d2e" custom_hover_background="#65656b" custom_color="#ffffff" custom_hover_color="#ffffff" border_radius="0px" font_size="14px" letter_spacing="1px"]Board Meeting Procedures[/vcex_button][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vcex_divider color="#d8d8d8"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1555596426318{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 20px !important;}" local_scroll_id="responsibilities"][vc_column][vc_tta_accordion style="modern" color="blue" spacing="10" c_icon="triangle" active_section="" collapsible_all="true" title="BOARD MEETING ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES"][vc_tta_section title="EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR RESPONSIBILITIES" tab_id="1460467547434-8a26f6be-f108"][vc_column_text]

The Executive Director needs to be someone in whom the board chair has faith that the organization is in good hands, and who is open to constructive – and even occasionally critical – feedback that can elevate the organization’s performance. Fulfilling these seemingly straightforward requirements can be surprisingly difficult for CEOs. This may help explain many of the complexities that can make successful partnerships between executive directors and board chairs a rarity. With all of this in mind, and with this critical relationship at stake, this blog-post seeks to outline some of the challenges and responsibilities of the executive director / CEO as they relate to the board in general, and the board chair in particular. 

Additional Resources:

What are the Executive Director Responsibilities?

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="NON-EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR RESPONSIBILITIES" tab_id="1460467548573-356d2e22-cd2e"][vc_column_text]

As a whole, the board is collectively responsible for moving the company towards forward progression by directing the company’s affairs. A Non-Executive Director shares many of the same responsibilities as an Executive Director, but he/she is not an employee of the company and is not a part of the executive management team. Non-executive Directors have the same legal duties and potential liabilities as their executive partners.

Regardless of the size of the company, a Non-Executive Director is someone who brings scope to the board, by offering a broad perspective of company and business issues, from someone who is independent from the day-to-day running of the company. Think of the Non-Executive Director as the eyes and ears of the business. The Institute of Directors notes that the Non-Executive Director brings objective criticism to the company. Additional Resources: What are the Non-Executive Director Responsibilities? [/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="BOARD MEMBER RESPONSIBILITIES" tab_id="1460467633490-37137045-0848"][vc_column_text]As a whole, the board of directors bears a legal responsibility to govern a corporation. Fulfilling that responsibility encompasses many individual roles and responsibilities. Each board member brings different strengths, talents, and abilities to the board. When board members merge their skills toward the mission and vision of an organization, it creates a synergy that makes the whole board greater than the sum of each individual’s contribution. Serving on a board requires time and dedication. Additional Resources: What are a Board Member's Responsibilities?[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="BOARD CHAIR RESPONSIBILITIES" tab_id="1460467668437-13f1bd2e-dc57"][vc_column_text]The Board Chair is often seen as a meeting facilitator. In reality, the Board Chair responsibilities are far greater than that. The Board Chair maintains focus on what is best for the company or organization. He/she facilitates good board leadership and governance and sets the tone for the meetings. Working collaboratively with the CEO or Executive Director, the Board Chair molds the board’s culture and work. An effective Board Chair influences the direction and priorities of the board. It’s an active role that engages the board members, building upon each member’s individual strengths. Additional Resources: What is the role of the Board Chair?[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="CORPORATE SECRETARY / BOARD LIASON RESPONSIBILITIES" tab_id="1460467723774-83e6abd9-ec84"][vc_column_text]The main responsibility of the Corporate Secretary is planning and preparing for meetings. At a minimum, this includes the following five areas: Scheduling, Agendas, Presentations, Executive Liaisons, and Documenting the Meeting. Additional Resources: What are the responsibilities of the Corporate Secretary or Board Liaison?[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/vc_tta_accordion][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1460468482029{margin-bottom: 20px !important;padding-top: 50px !important;}" local_scroll_id="effective"][vc_column][vc_tta_accordion style="modern" color="blue" spacing="10" c_icon="triangle" active_section="" collapsible_all="true" title="RUNNING AN EFFECTIVE BOARD MEETING"][vc_tta_section title="BOARD MEETING AGENDA" tab_id="1460467959414-c5de577f-32ec"][vc_column_text]It’s a rare meeting where the board of directors has enough time to accomplish everything that it needs to. Having an established and focused board meeting agenda helps the board maximize accuracy, efficiency, and productivity. Board meeting agendas include items for managing routine business and for tackling special projects. Additional Resources: Board Meeting Agenda Format and Template How to Hold the Greatest Board Meeting Ever How to Take Minutes at a Board Meeting What is a Consent Agenda for a Board Meeting[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="COMMON BOARD MEETING MISTAKES" tab_id="1460467960039-7f732f80-b41e"][vc_column_text]The work of boards is incredibly important but also complex. The work of boards has many potentially destructive forces that haunt them. Boards are plagued by their own forces of destruction, which can wreak havoc on their work. These common board dysfunctions could comprise the “Four Horsemen of the Board Apocalypse,” represented by Waste, Fear, Boredom, and Addiction. Besides the board dysfunctions described above, it is now more important than ever before that your board of directors is highly engaged in the mission and business of your organization. Over the past decade, the bar has been raised on board performance – it’s no longer sufficient (if it ever was) for board members to simply show up to meetings, nod their heads in agreement, and go home. Your stakeholders want tangible evidence that your organization is fulfilling its mission. Your board members – as the owners of your organization’s mission – are in the crosshairs of this scrutiny. Board engagement is critical. Although engagement is absolutely critical to governance, we still see many of the same mistakes made by boards. Additional Resources: The 4 Horsemen of the (Board) Apocalypse 7 Ways to Destroy Board Engagement[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="HOW CAN TECHNOLOGY HELP?" tab_id="1460468123067-0752db12-883e"][vc_column_text]In much of life, less is more. This is true when it comes to the length of speeches, weeks of winter, consumption of natural resources, and strokes in golf (to name only a few examples). This is also true in regards to paper in the board room. This prior BoardEffect post offers a valuable framework and lays out some of the key considerations for HOW to manage the transition to Becoming a Paperless Board. Let us take a step back and pause to consider WHY a board would want to hold paperless meetings in the first place. Read more! Additional Resources: How to Sell Board Management Software to your Board Leveraging Technology to Elevate Board Performance Learn More about using a Board Portal How to Hold the Greatest Board Meeting Ever[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="HELPFUL TIPS" tab_id="1468010145017-029fe185-9807"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_message]

5 tips for opening a board meeting:

  1. Allow time for members to get settled and focused.
  2. Provide a way for members to share what's weighing on their minds.
  3. Include time for socializing
  4. Clarify each person's specific role for the meeting.
  5. Take time to formally review and approve the agenda.
[/vc_message][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_message]

5 tips for running a board meeting:

  1. Start and end on time
  2. Ensure full participation, by all members
  3. Favor group discussion over "reporting"
  4. Tap into each member's unique expertise
  5. Stick to Robert's Rules for ease and fairness
[/vc_message][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_tta_section][/vc_tta_accordion][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1555596435699{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 20px !important;}" local_scroll_id="procedures"][vc_column][vc_tta_accordion style="modern" shape="square" color="blue" gap="10" c_icon="triangle" active_section="" collapsible_all="true" title="BOARD MEETING PROCEDURES"][vc_tta_section title="NOTICE OF BOARD MEETING" tab_id="1460467023466-1fcd1b15-9aee"][vc_column_text]Some of the minor duties of the board are so routine that they seem insignificant and perhaps, borderline annoying. The risk in not providing a timely notice of a board meeting is that if all of the directors cannot attend, those who were unable to attend may try to overturn the decisions that were made at the meeting. They may even have the right to demand a second meeting and no one will be happy with that. The bylaws rule on whether the meeting notice has to be in writing or whether the notice can be sent by electronic or other means. Look to best practices to set a “reasonable” timeframe. This means giving enough time for directors to decide whether or not to attend the meeting and time to prepare documents for the meeting and agenda. Additional Resources: Notice of the Board Meeting: Regular and Special What are the Responsibilities of the Board Secretary or Board Liaison? What is Board Meeting Protocol? Planning a Board Meeting: A How-to Guide[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="QUORUM" tab_id="1460467024014-32c280ea-db74"][vc_column_text]The purpose of a quorum is two-fold—to make sure that board decisions are made by majority vote and to prevent a tie-vote of the board members. A common requirement for a board quorum is for 2/3 of board members to be present to conduct official business, though the bylaws may state any number. One of the first duties of the board chair is to determine if a quorum is present. Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised offers a suggestion on how to set the rules for a quorum. It states that the quorum “should approximate the largest number that can be depended on to attend any meeting except in very bad weather or other extremely unfavorable conditions." Additional Resources: What Constitutes a Quorum How to Chair a Board Meeting What is Board Meeting Protocol?[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="DEALING WITH MOTIONS" tab_id="1460467199502-c6cec964-8087"][vc_column_text]The board chair is primarily responsible for dealing with motions. To keep things democratic, board members have an equal responsibility for knowing how motions should be managed and for speaking up when protocol isn’t being followed. All board members need to understand the purpose, function, and protocol for various kinds of motions including main motions, subsidiary motions, privileged motions, and incidental motions. Clear motions equal clear actions! Additional Resources: How to Write a Motion for a Board Meeting What is Board Meeting Protocol? Managing Motions in Parliamentary Procedure How to Use Incidental Motions Subsidiary Motions: A List of the 7 Types Privileged Motions: A Few Types and Examples[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="VOTING PROCEDURES" tab_id="1460467255276-6b39a813-6ae3"][vc_column_text]The board chair has the responsibility to clearly state a motion before the board. The chair asks for “yea” or “yes” votes and then “nay” or “no” votes. Board members usually give a voice vote, but votes can also be signified with a show of hands, standing to rise, or by ballot. Some bylaws require a vote by roll call. The board chair may elect to retake a vote when the results aren’t clear. Additional Resources: Research Report: U.S. Laws Governing Nonprofit Boards and Electronic Voting How to Write a Motion for a Board Meeting[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/vc_tta_accordion][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row typography_style="white" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554823657157{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 50px !important;background-color: #194f7d !important;}"][vc_column css_animation="fadeInUp" el_class="testimonial"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1554823681269{margin-top: 35px !important;}"]

Based on the function and price comparison BoardEffect was easily seen as the best solution. We have been pleased with our implementation and our ongoing support by BoardEffect. BoardEffect has a wide install base that gives them the experience to guide implementation decisions for best practice with their portal.”

Vice President, Chief Information Officer, Ohio Presbyterian Retirement Services

item.content:encoded:
[vc_row][vc_column][rev_slider_vc alias="unt-case-study"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465914506728{margin-top: 50px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="Client Challenge" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1462565635692{margin-top: 50px !important;margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

The University of North Texas System had a system for distributing board materials electronically, but most regents refused to use it, instead printing out board books of 800-plus pages for each meeting. They found the electronic books difficult to navigate and impossible to annotate, according to system administrator Lindsey Vandagriff. And they felt the overall tool was clunky and frustrating.

Assembling printed board books took extraordinary time and effort. Information had to be presented in precisely the order in which it would be discussed and revisited, resulting in hundreds of pages of redundant content. Moreover, each iteration of the books required multiple sign-offs from leaders in the university system.

Given the cumbersome assembly process, materials often weren’t available for regents to review before a meeting. Vandagriff and the board secretary set out to find a more efficient, user-friendly alternative—and a system regents would actually use.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" typography_style="white" css=".vc_custom_1462564674835{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 50px !important;background-color: #1a4e7d !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="The BoardEffect Solution" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%23ffffff" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465913899676{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1465913922397{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]

Their search led to the robust, intuitive BoardEffect portal. Not only did BoardEffect make board books accessible on mobile devices, it addressed the immediate concerns of annotation, navigation, and assembly.

BoardEffect’s bookmarking and pagination features let regents move back and forth easily among pages and sections. Because information no longer needed to be duplicated for the flow of discussion, the size of board books decreased: from an average of 830 pages to 500-600.

Of course, even the best solution is of limited value if people refuse to use it. That’s why Vandagriff was pleased to see buy-in for BoardEffect from the start. During an on-site training for system administrators, one regent who had been particularly loyal to paper and pen chose to participate and enjoyed the experience.

“It was good for the regent to see that we were learning, too,” Vandagriff said.

Despite some initial hesitations about new software and tablets, the rest of the organization adopted BoardEffect quickly. Regents soon found it easy to access and annotate board materials from any device.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1442770270768{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="The Impact" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465913932770{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1465916114720{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]

It’s unbelievable how much stress BoardEffect has taken out of the equation

Not only did BoardEffect’s annotation and navigation functions stop regents from preferring paper board books, the tool changed the process of creating board books. No longer were cumbersome sign-offs needed for multiple iterations of the same document. In fact, the administrative team now is able to publish all materials in advance of board meetings.

“It’s unbelievable how much stress BoardEffect has taken out of the equation,” Vandagriff said. She added that the team “now has a clearer process for pre-board meeting work, and that’s a huge component of what makes the meeting successful.”

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" column_spacing="40" css=".vc_custom_1465914040719{padding-top: 50px !important;background-color: #dfe0e8 !important;}"][vc_column width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="8578" alignment="center"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][vc_custom_heading text="Tips" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1462564580115{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1465913601099{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]To use BoardEffect most effectively, Vandagriff advised that organizations:
  • Start by learning the preferences, pain points, IT comfort levels, and learning styles of each board member. She suggested administering an online or paper survey and using BoardEffect to tabulate the data.
  • Let board members make their own discoveries—don’t push them. When a reluctant regent heard a colleague boast about his iPad annotations, he reached out for guidance “and quickly ran with it,” Vandagriff said.
  • Realize that higher-quality materials are just one ingredient of better board meetings. You need strong communication and internal processes as well, she said, particularly before a board meeting.
Remember that enthusiasm is contagious. “Let board members teach each other about their areas of expertise,” she said, “and soon all will be exploring what they can do in the platform.”[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" typography_style="white" css=".vc_custom_1461540866063{padding-top: 40px !important;padding-bottom: 40px !important;background-color: #822054 !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="Get The Case Study" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%23ffffff" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1462823417937{margin-bottom: 15px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1462823407936{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]

Click the button below to download our case study for the University of North Texas.

Board governance is complex, demanding, and high-stakes. BoardEffect supports best practices within and across each cycle of board activity. This, coupled with BoardEffect's state of the art approach to security and services, sets us apart in the industry.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_single_image image="19683" img_size="900x360" alignment="center"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554664843526{padding-top: 75px !important;padding-bottom: 50px !important;}" local_scroll_id="focusedonsecurity"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="Focused On Security" font_container="tag:h2|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554139727132{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

The Board's work is not only important; it’s often sensitive, confidential and even controversial. The BoardEffect secure board portal is at the vanguard in terms of data security and discoverability, offering organizations the opportunity to be intentional with the security of their platforms by allowing them to manage settings and control the level of access that meets their objectives. Our commitment to flexibility of configuration extends to product security and meets the NIST 2014 Cybersecurity Standard framework, trusted by financial institutions and other organizations that depend on strict data protection.

BoardEffect provides a multi-layered defense to protect sensitive board information through our security program in a state of the art dedicated SOC2 infrastructure.

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554664856598{padding-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3" css=".vc_custom_1443542161485{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Data Recovery" heading_type="h3" icon="icon-Data_Recovery" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="64px" classes="equal-height-content" icon_bottom_margin="35px"]

item.title: Webinar: How to Get Your Board "Onboard" and Aligned
item.dc:creator: Jbarlow
item.content:encoded:
[vc_row column_spacing="60" equal_height="yes" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1555000078846{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 25px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="How to Get Your Board ``Onboard`` and Aligned" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1463061902380{margin-top: 25px !important;margin-bottom: 10px !important;}"][vc_video link="https://vimeo.com/166364545/610bc4b537" css=".vc_custom_1463061572500{margin-top: 50px !important;}"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1457102275466{margin-bottom: 100px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_column_text]Your board members are an extension of your organization, and just like you and your team, they are best equipped to support and propel your mission forward when they are strategically aligned. However, this can often be easier said than done, which is why Plenty and BoardEffect have joined forces to guide you through this critical, and sometimes complex process. Join our teams for an exclusive webinar on how to create alignment with and within your board. During this 60-minute webinar our teams will explore the following:
  • What true alignment is, why it matters, and how to recognize when it’s missing
  • How you can use strategic planning to create alignment and the steps to get started
  • An introduction to the tools you can use to reinforce your strategy once it’s created

We don’t limit the hours you can contact us. Nor will you incur additional fees when you do need our help. Relentless Care knows no limits.

Whether it’s a last minute training for your board of trustees or a question about how to use the polling feature in BoardEffect, our team of experts is here to provide Relentless Care for you. That’s our promise; and your success is what drives us.

item.title: BOARD DOCUMENT MANAGEMENT
item.dc:creator: Primer
item.content:encoded:
[vc_row][vc_column][rev_slider_vc alias="board-document-management"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1463758672363{margin-bottom: 50px !important;padding-top: 100px !important;}" local_scroll_id="approach"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="Board Document Management Software" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554140555706{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

Boards that still use the print and mail method for board document management see less engaged boards and experience document distribution challenges as well as higher costs. BoardEffect's board document management software allows for easy-to-use, secure hosting, creation and distribution of board documents for simplified board meeting preparation, increased collaboration,  and lower costs by going paperless.

[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/board-portal/" size="medium" title="SEE FEATURES" style="flat" align="center" css_wrap=".vc_custom_1554213737937{margin-top: 50px !important;}" classes="green"]See Features[/vcex_button][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1463760316553{padding-top: 100px !important;background-color: #dfe0e8 !important;}" local_scroll_id="paperless"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="Benefits Of Paperless Board Meetings" font_container="tag:h2|text_align:center" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554140585109{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1464046596844{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"]

The development of the BoardEffect platform is guided by principles which reflect the values or character we aspire for our solution to embody. These concepts work in concert with each other to deliver a high level of user engagement.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1463758352001{background-color: #dfe0e8 !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3" css=".vc_custom_1442847940380{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Document Management" heading_type="h3" icon="fa fa-archive" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="30px" classes="equal-height-content" icon_bottom_margin="35px"]

Manage all board documents online from electronic board books, minutes, agendas and more. Then easily distribute to your board in one-click.

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3" css=".vc_custom_1442847947197{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Simple Framework" heading_type="h3" icon="fa fa-check-circle" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="30px" classes="equal-height-content" icon_bottom_margin="35px"]

BoardEffect provides the structure and framework, complemented by a rich resource library full of sample documents, to assist board members in transcending the meeting-to-meeting responsibilities while elevating organizational effectiveness.

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3" css=".vc_custom_1443552505350{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Collaboration" heading_type="h3" icon="fa fa-users" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="30px" classes="equal-height-content" icon_bottom_margin="35px"]

BoardEffect plays a central role in enabling collaboration among board members and improving connectivity across the board cycles.

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1463758471555{padding-bottom: 50px !important;background-color: #dfe0e8 !important;}"][vc_column width="1/2" css=".vc_custom_1442847940380{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Structure & Hierarchy" heading_type="h3" icon="fa fa-sliders" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="30px" css=".vc_custom_1464094676594{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}" classes="equal-height-content" icon_bottom_margin="35px"]

Enable a clear board structure and information hierarchy. Permissions allow for only certain members to see certain information.

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2" css=".vc_custom_1442847947197{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Search" heading_type="h3" icon="fa fa-search" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="30px" classes="equal-height-content" icon_bottom_margin="35px"]

A robust search function allows board members to easily find current and past documents and information through simple file descriptions.

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1463760817888{margin-bottom: 100px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="Ready To Go Paperless?" font_container="tag:h2|text_align:center" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554140602738{padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 30px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1463760837946{padding-bottom: 30px !important;}"]

See a short demo of how the our paperless board meeting solution will help streamline your board meetings for better results.

item.title: Nonprofits Laws: Board Rules and Regulations
item.dc:creator: Primer
item.content:encoded:
[vc_row typography_style="white" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465238598091{padding-top: 40px !important;background-color: #1a4e7d !important;}"][vc_column][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="30" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1466114392774{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;}" el_id="board-portal-head"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="NONPROFIT LAWS: BOARD RULES AND REGULATIONS" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1470255985851{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]

Released August 2016

[/vc_column_text][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1470257466409{margin-bottom: 75px !important;}"]

Though this study was just released, the initial research began years ago with the simple question “Can nonprofit boards legally vote online?” The intent was to determine the legal parameters within which a board could use board portal technology to manage its voting procedures.  In response, BoardEffect published a March 2012 research report titled “U.S. Laws Governing Nonprofit Boards and Electronic Voting.”

Since that time, there has been widespread adoption of board portals by nonprofit organizations, with online voting representing a core board activity.  Nevertheless, questions persist regarding the legality of online voting, with many new questions and concerns arising as board portal adoption becomes increasingly pervasive.  Uncertainty in this area has also grown as nonprofits seek to navigate a rapidly evolving legal, technical, and governance landscape.

It is with all of this in mind, that BoardEffect has updated and significantly expanded its initial research in this field.  This latest scope of work focuses on answering recurring questions among nonprofit boards regarding the legal ramifications of utilizing technology.

The resulting study captures findings from this research. We hope to help inform our clients and others on the state laws that should be reviewed and understood in the context of implementing board management software.

We chose the following 13 topic areas to survey in the Study because we believe these board activities are reasonably supported by the functions of board portal technology.  For a detailed look at how we define these terms, see below.

[/vc_column_text][vc_tta_accordion style="flat" shape="square" gap="10" c_icon="triangle" c_position="right" active_section="15" no_fill="true" collapsible_all="true"][vc_tta_section title="Actions" tab_id="1465241058970-a54e3247-e9b1"][vc_column_text]Actions refer to votes or any decision that requires the input of the full board.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Conflict of Interest" tab_id="1465241225580-384e6ac3-469a"][vc_column_text]Refers to the actions of board members that have a material interest – whether direct or indirect – in an issue being decided by the board.  An example of a conflict of interest might be a board member who is a senior officer of a company with which the nonprofit is considering doing business.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Election by Directors" tab_id="1465241201828-51e049af-5f91"][vc_column_text]Refers to the way new board members are selected/approved to serve a term on the board.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="E-Meetings, including E-voting" tab_id="1465241030874-6fdaeba9-a2bb"][vc_column_text]Refers to the use of technology other than hard-copy mail used in board communications, including meeting notice, voting, approvals, and other common board communications.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Meeting Location" tab_id="1465240924951-eba0b810-f629"][vc_column_text]Refers to the physical/virtual location where regular and special board meetings may occur.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Notice of Meeting" tab_id="1465240955291-253454f1-69aa"][vc_column_text]Refers to the requirement of organizations to alert board members in advance of the date, time, and location for a board meeting.  The provisions in Notice of Meeting and Waiver of Notice also define what constitutes “notice.”[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Quorum" tab_id="1465239086041-fd38aefd-d964"][vc_column_text]Establishes the minimum number of voting members that must be present at a meeting in order for a vote to occur.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Removal" tab_id="1465241180910-be66c168-60fd"][vc_column_text]Refers to the termination – by the organization – of a board member’s service on the board.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Residency" tab_id="1465239085885-aecb761a-2b2b"][vc_column_text]Refers to legal provisions requiring nonprofit boards members to reside in the same state where the nonprofit is incorporated.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Resignation" tab_id="1465241198893-b383f799-50c0"][vc_column_text]Refers to the termination – by the board member – of the board member’s service on the board.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Terms & Limits" tab_id="1465240858853-71ab8644-1aad"][vc_column_text]Refers to the number of years a board member serves in a single term, and any provisions in the state code to limit the number of terms (consecutive or non-consecutive) a member may serve.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Vacancy" tab_id="1465241103374-7a189a8b-0a1d"][vc_column_text]Refers to a seat on the board – as outlined in the organization’s bylaws – that is not currently filled by a member.  The vacancy could occur due to resignation, removal, or attrition.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Waiver of Notice" tab_id="1465240998384-6be55761-eccc"][vc_column_text]Refers to the rights of board members to “waive” their right to be notified in advance of board meetings, and to the conditions under which an organization would not need to provide advance notice of a board meeting.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/vc_tta_accordion][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="60" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1466641883002{padding-top: 75px What are the range of options taken on the topic of board member residency requirements? How does my state provide for the use of technology in board communications, including meeting notice, voting, and approvals?

[vc_row][vc_column][rev_slider_vc alias="field-guide-v-3"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" match_column_height="yes" column_spacing="60" css=".vc_custom_1444338584743{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 100px !important;}"][vc_column width="2/3"][vc_custom_heading text="New Guide: Leveraging Technology to Elevate Board Performance" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:left|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1446660875912{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

Over the last two decades, governance — the work performed by boards of directors – has become a more challenging endeavor than ever before. Overwhelmingly, resources are scarcer, requiring organizations to do more with less.

Scandals in the corporate, public and nonprofit sectors have resulted in increased pressure and scrutiny on boards of directors from regulators and stakeholders alike. In this environment, boards and staff are seeking ways to perform at a higher level by operating in an agile manner. And yet, most of the prescriptive literature on board governance tends more toward the theoretical than the practical. This leaves board members relatively unsupported in their quest to effect lasting change for their organizations, sometimes in environments that can actually discourage innovation. The purpose of this field guide is to confront these important challenges head-on. The guide focuses on three below key thematic competencies that are common among high-performing boards, and explores the meaning and importance of each.
  • Part 1. Enhancing Board Processes: Where the rubber meets the road
  • Part 2. Channeling Strategic Collaboration: The grease that allows the engine run
  • Part 3. Fostering Circumspect Vision: Navigating through the windshield and rear-view

item.content:encoded:
[vc_row][vc_column][rev_slider_vc alias="revised_american_public_media_case_study"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465914506728{margin-top: 50px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="Client Challenge" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%23194f7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554396154493{margin-top: 50px !important;margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

The distribution process was extraordinarily time-consuming.

American Public Media, the nation's largest owner and operator of public radio stations and producer and distributor of premier national programming, recognized the need for an electronic option for conducting business with its Board of Trustees in 2012, even before board portals achieved widespread popularity. “Like many organizations, we were killing too many trees as we produced huge amounts of board meeting materials,” explains JoAnn Cragoe, Executive Assistant to the President. “The distribution process was extraordinarily time-consuming.” Not only did meeting prep drain internal resources (paper and staff time), but also significant resources on the receiving end, as costly Fed Ex and local courier services delivered materials to board members in advance of meetings.

At the time, whatever version of the meeting materials that got distributed was considered final, even if changes were necessary. Board members were unable to receive updates or revisions until a separate email was sent or they arrived at the meetings.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row typography_style="white" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1554396182508{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;padding-top: 50px !important;padding-bottom: 50px !important;background-color: #194f7d !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="The BoardEffect Solution" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%23ffffff" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465913899676{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1469454654921{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]

We are a nonprofit company and we liked that BoardEffect understands the needs of nonprofit organizations. That, and the fact that BoardEffect is fairly priced, really appealed to us.

Having vetted four or five other platforms, American Public Media chose BoardEffect, but not just because it provided tremendous flexibility for delivering and receiving materials. As JoAnn explains, “we are a nonprofit company and we liked that BoardEffect understands the needs of nonprofit organizations. That, and the fact that BoardEffect is fairly priced, really appealed to us.”

Now, board members use BoardEffect on their PCs or via the dedicated iPad app to access materials before meetings with – as JoAnn emphasizes --“ease and gratitude that they don’t have to deal with a hard copy and have the materials available at all times, wherever they are. Delivery of board materials is immediate and easy.”

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1442770270768{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="The Impact" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465913932770{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1554396196084{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]

I didn’t realize how much of an impact the easy delivery of board materials would have.

Using BoardEffect has made a big difference. As JoAnn explains, “I didn’t realize how much of an impact the easy delivery of board materials would have.”  Board members are prepared and find the system user-friendly and dependable. When the organization implemented BoardEffect in 2012, most board members were content with a paper version of materials, explains JoAnn. Now they can easily make hard copies if they chose, “though I can’t think of any reason we would ever move away from an electronic portal, we are permanent converts!”

She continues, “we might be a little slow to consistently use other functions BoardEffect makes available to its users, but we recently conducted a Board self-evaluation survey on BoardEffect and it was easy to use. The function enabled us to develop quickly a professional looking report on results that included the details we needed.  With the acceptance of technology that newer board members bring and expect, we hope to soon be using all the other tools BoardEffect provides.”

Even after BoardEffect’s recent platform upgrade, JoAnn “was surprised by how few questions there were from board members about access.” She also was surprised by how many now use multiple BoardEffect apps for other boards they serve – “that wasn’t true in the beginning.”

JoAnn acknowledges the upgrade required her to spend some time figuring things out because her understanding of technology tends to be the result of effort and management of a learning curve, rather than intuitive. “But not everyone is like that,” she offers, “and I’m here to tell you that even those of us who have been around awhile can become BoardEffect experts and find using it to be FUN!”

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1442770270768{margin-top: 100px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vcex_divider][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row column_spacing="40" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1555593185720{padding-top: 50px !important;}"][vc_column width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="9098" alignment="center"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][vc_custom_heading text="Tips" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:left|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1462564580115{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1465915739071{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]To use BoardEffect most effectively, JoAnn advises that organizations:
  • Leverage the knowledge center in the platform. As someone who still prefers paper to video (in part because watching a video requires a commitment of uninterrupted time), she initially printed instructions for creating a meeting book and the board survey. She eventually took time to watch the BoardEffect videos and webinars and found them very useful.
  • Expand the team of administrators. Initially JoAnn was the sole administrator for the board and its committees. Since then, other staff have been trained to manage specific areas within the platform so they can distribute meeting materials and handle other functions.
  • Ask for help. JoAnn has seen the impact of BoardEffect’s investment in helpdesk personnel over the years APM has been a client. “It’s fantastic to get service right away from a live person when I have questions and the helpdesk staff is helpful, knowledgeable and totally client-friendly.”
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row typography_style="white" center_row="yes" css=".vc_custom_1600267283914{padding-top: 40px !important;padding-bottom: 40px !important;background-color: #7c7c7c !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="REQUEST A DEMO" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:32|text_align:center|color:%23ffffff" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1469808422226{margin-bottom: 15px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

item.title: Research Approach
item.dc:creator: Primer
item.content:encoded:
[vc_row center_row="yes" typography_style="white" css=".vc_custom_1465238598091{padding-top: 40px !important;background-color: #1a4e7d !important;}"][vc_column][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" column_spacing="40" css=".vc_custom_1466113788132{margin-top: 50px !important;margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="BACKGROUND" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:24px|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1466521956188{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1466943569845{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"]

In 2013, New York passed a sweeping set of legal reforms governing the actions of the boards of New York State’s private nonprofits. The law, known as the Nonprofit Revitalization Act, was designed in part to streamline and modernize New York State’s Not for Profit Corporation Law, including:

[/vc_column_text][vcex_list_item font_family="Open Sans" text_align="center" icon="fa fa-check" font_size="16px" font_color="#1d3f7d" color="#aec03d" css=".vc_custom_1466014488491{margin-bottom: 20px !important;}"]provisions for electronic submissions of audit[/vcex_list_item][vcex_list_item font_family="Open Sans" text_align="center" icon="fa fa-check" font_size="16px" font_color="#1d3f7d" color="#aec03d" css=".vc_custom_1466014495634{margin-bottom: 20px !important;}"]electronic voting and meetings held remotely by nonprofit boards, and[/vcex_list_item][vcex_list_item font_family="Open Sans" text_align="center" icon="fa fa-check" font_size="16px" font_color="#1d3f7d" color="#aec03d" css=".vc_custom_1466014503341{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"]reducing the number of classifications of nonprofits in the state.[/vcex_list_item][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1472222334017{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"]

The law also increased the requirements being placed on New York’s nonprofit boards to ensure ethical standards of behavior, including provisions related to Conflicts of Interest and Whistleblower Protection, that are correlates to components of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act governing the boards of publicly-traded corporations. New York’s Nonprofit Revitalization Act represented a new high-water mark in terms of regulation of nonprofit boards – and provided legal weight behind what are widely considered to be best practices for nonprofit boards. It also raised the stakes on the questions outlined above, moving many to question the degree to which their own state’s laws measured up to NY’s Nonprofit Revitalization Act. Meanwhile, from the perspective of BoardEffect, it was critical to understand the ways in which state laws might impact how our clients could legally utilize board portals to support the work of their boards. In other words, in what ways do state laws impact usage of software like BoardEffect for nonprofit boards?

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" column_spacing="40" css=".vc_custom_1465240046057{padding-top: 75px !important;padding-bottom: 75px !important;background-color: #dfe0e8 !important;}" local_scroll_id="development"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="RESEARCH APPROACH" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:24px|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465239258051{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1469736101781{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"]

In 2013, the state of New York significantly revised the set of laws governing its nonprofits.  This prompted us to review those changes and begin contemplating the implications of the NYS Nonprofit Revitalization Act on other states.  Subsequently, BoardEffect decided to research the way in which every state in the U.S. governs board actions.

To do so, BoardEffect conducted an exhaustive review of the current legal codes governing private, nonprofit boards on a state by state basis. However, this was not an exhaustive review of all laws relating to nonprofits.  Rather, this review was confined to the activities of boards that we believed to be reasonably supported by the functions of board portal technology. To establish this benchmark, we turned to the BoardEffect Product Framework, which drives how the BoardEffect solution is developed.

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading text="BoardEffect Product Framework" font_container="tag:h3|font_size:18px|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes"][vc_single_image image="9911" img_size="875x300" alignment="center" css=".vc_custom_1469829868420{margin-top: 35px !important;margin-bottom: 75px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1469736084478{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"]

Specifically, the work of boards is complex, demanding, and high-stakes. It is also cyclical in nature. Boards convene on a regular meeting cycle, deliver on a recurring set of annual responsibilities, and continuously work to refresh and strengthen themselves as strategic assets to the organizations they serve. These activities occur within three different operating cycles, each with its own pace and components. BoardEffect’s product vision and corresponding feature roadmap are driven by boards’ responsibilities across these demanding, interdependent, and mission critical cycles.  Moreover, this framework and BoardEffect’s product capabilities can be leveraged to manage the topics addressed in this study as follows:

[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading text="Nonprofit Laws Topic Areas" font_container="tag:h3|font_size:18px|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes"][vc_single_image image="9912" img_size="875x300" alignment="center" css=".vc_custom_1469829882452{margin-top: 35px !important;margin-bottom: 75px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

As we did in our first report on “U.S. Laws Governing Electronic Voting by Nonprofit Boards,” our first step was to connect with the offices in each state responsible for regulating charities. Thankfully, many states have improved online access to their legal codes and provisions a great deal since our first report in 2012. Most of the data presented in this study was collected simply by visiting each state’s website and locating the most current laws governing nonprofit corporations. However, when that was not possible, or when we were not able to clearly identify how current the information available online might be, we reached out directly to the state offices for guidance.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" column_spacing="40" css=".vc_custom_1467125574962{margin-top: 70px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="AUTHORS" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:24px|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" column_spacing="40" css=".vc_custom_1467125559302{margin-bottom: 50px !important;}"][vc_column width="1/3"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Todd Gibby" icon="fa fa-pencil" icon_bottom_margin="20px" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="40px" heading_size="18px" url="/todd-gibby/"]

CEO

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Dottie Schindlinger" icon="fa fa-pencil" icon_bottom_margin="20px" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="40px" heading_size="18px" url="/dottie-schindlinger/"]

EVP / Governance Technology Evangelist

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][vcex_icon_box style="two" alignment="center" heading="Isabelle Clérié" icon="fa fa-pencil" icon_bottom_margin="20px" heading_color="#1a4e7d" icon_color="#1a4e7d" icon_size="40px" heading_size="18px" url="https://boardeffect.com/isabelle-clerie/"]

Research Consultant

[/vcex_icon_box][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" column_spacing="60" css=".vc_custom_1466641883002{padding-top: 75px !important;padding-bottom: 25px !important;background-color: #dfe0e8 !important;}"][vc_column][vcex_icon icon="fa fa-file-pdf-o" float="center" color="#1a4e7d"][vc_custom_heading text="STUDY BRIEF" font_container="tag:h1|font_size:24|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1469535762242{margin-top: 25px !important;margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1466712193372{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]

Download the Nonprofit Laws: Board Rules and Regulations Study Brief to share with anyone involved in supporting the work of nonprofit organizations.

[/vc_column_text][vcex_button url="/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/BoardEffect_Nonprofit_Laws-Board_Rules_and_Regulations.pdf" title="DOWNLOAD" style="flat" align="center" size="medium"]DOWNLOAD[/vcex_button][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" column_spacing="60" css=".vc_custom_1465925437866{margin-top: 75px !important;margin-bottom: 75px !important;}"][vc_column][vc_custom_heading text="DEFINITIONS OF TERMS USED IN THIS STUDY" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:24px|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1466521786268{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1468419338936{margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"]

We chose the following 13 topic areas to survey in the Study because we believe these board activities are reasonably supported by the functions of board portal technology.  For a detailed look at how we define these terms, see below.

[/vc_column_text][vc_tta_accordion style="flat" shape="square" gap="10" c_icon="triangle" c_position="right" active_section="15" no_fill="true" collapsible_all="true"][vc_tta_section title="Actions" tab_id="1465241058970-a54e3247-e9b1"][vc_column_text]Actions refer to votes or any decision that requires the input of the full board.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Conflict of Interest" tab_id="1465241225580-384e6ac3-469a"][vc_column_text]Refers to the actions of board members that have a material interest – whether direct or indirect – in an issue being decided by the board.  An example of a conflict of interest might be a board member who is a senior officer of a company with which the nonprofit is considering doing business.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Election by Directors" tab_id="1465241201828-51e049af-5f91"][vc_column_text]Refers to the way new board members are selected/approved to serve a term on the board.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="E-Meetings, including E-voting" tab_id="1465241030874-6fdaeba9-a2bb"][vc_column_text]Refers to the use of technology other than hard-copy mail used in board communications, including meeting notice, voting, approvals, and other common board communications.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Meeting Location" tab_id="1465240924951-eba0b810-f629"][vc_column_text]Refers to the physical/virtual location where regular and special board meetings may occur.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Notice of Meeting" tab_id="1465240955291-253454f1-69aa"][vc_column_text]Refers to the requirement of organizations to alert board members in advance of the date, time, and location for a board meeting.  The provisions in Notice of Meeting and Waiver of Notice also define what constitutes “notice.”[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Quorum" tab_id="1465239086041-fd38aefd-d964"][vc_column_text]Establishes the minimum number of voting members that must be present at a meeting in order for a vote to occur.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Removal" tab_id="1465241180910-be66c168-60fd"][vc_column_text]Refers to the termination – by the organization – of a board member’s service on the board.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Residency" tab_id="1465239085885-aecb761a-2b2b"][vc_column_text]Refers to legal provisions requiring nonprofit boards members to reside in the same state where the nonprofit is incorporated.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Resignation" tab_id="1465241198893-b383f799-50c0"][vc_column_text]Refers to the termination – by the board member – of the board member’s service on the board.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Terms & Limits" tab_id="1465240858853-71ab8644-1aad"][vc_column_text]Refers to the number of years a board member serves in a single term, and any provisions in the state code to limit the number of terms (consecutive or non-consecutive) a member may serve.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Vacancy" tab_id="1465241103374-7a189a8b-0a1d"][vc_column_text]Refers to a seat on the board – as outlined in the organization’s bylaws – that is not currently filled by a member.  The vacancy could occur due to resignation, removal, or attrition.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Waiver of Notice " tab_id="1465240998384-6be55761-eccc"][vc_column_text]Refers to the rights of board members to “waive” their right to be notified in advance of board meetings, and to the conditions under which an organization would not need to provide advance notice of a board meeting.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/vc_tta_accordion][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row center_row="yes" column_spacing="40" css=".vc_custom_1466719708324{margin-top: 50px !important;margin-bottom: 75px !important;}"][vc_column][vcex_divider][vc_custom_heading text="DISCLAIMER" font_container="tag:h2|font_size:24px|text_align:center|color:%231a4e7d" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=".vc_custom_1465925543639{margin-top: 50px !important;margin-bottom: 35px !important;}"][vc_column_text]

This study represents a compilation to the best of our ability of the information available through public records on U.S. state laws concerning electronic voting and other areas of responsibility of nonprofit boards. The information contained in this study does not represent legal advice of any kind and should not be used in lieu of legal counsel. This study does not supersede any organization’s own bylaws; nor does it supersede any current local, state or federal laws in the U.S., nor laws of any countries outside the U.S. In addition, due to the constantly changing nature of online records, we cannot guarantee that the links to related websites listed are current.
